question: whats the difference between a major, a minor and a certificate at ramapo?

body.answer:
A major is required for every undergraduate degree. Its requirements are at least 40 and no more than 64 credits, including major-specific concentrations, tracks, and prerequisites; they typically make up about half of the degree program. [9]

A minor is supplemental and distinct from the major, adding depth and breadth to an undergraduate degree. It must include 16–24 credits; no more than half of its required credits may also count toward a primary or secondary major. [8]

An academic certificate is a coherent program of study, usually made up of credit-bearing courses; it may also include non-credit learning experiences. Certificates can be undergraduate, graduate, or doctoral. Graduate certificates require at least 9 credits beyond the bachelor’s level, and doctoral certificates require at least 12 beyond the master’s level. Certificates are not graduation requirements and are removed from the degree audit. [7]

Sources: [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#certificate-programs1) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [9](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1)

Global Communication and Media also requires COMM 203, 232 and 267; COMM 234, 266 and 318; one media production course; two media criticism/analysis courses; two media writing courses; one capstone portfolio course; and one elective. [1]

question: I'm a transfer student with 60 credits from community college. which gen ed requirements does Ramapo still make me take?

If at least 48 of your credits are from an accredited institution, Ramapo’s transfer-student rule requires Critical Reading and Writing 102, Quantitative Reasoning, Scientific Reasoning, and one course in each of two distribution categories: Culture and Creativity, Values and Ethics, and Social Systems and Society. Your exact remaining courses depend on the transfer evaluation and advisement; during academic advisement, you’ll be advised of applicable waivers and remaining requirements. If you completed an A.A. or A.S. at a New Jersey community college, Admissions says you are waived from General Education requirements after submitting a final official transcript showing the conferred degree. [12] Another page says an A.A. or A.S. from a New Jersey community college fulfills Gen Ed for a four-year Ramapo degree. [13] An A.A.S. does not qualify for a full waiver; courses are evaluated individually. [12]

Office of the Provost: provost@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7330. [10] Admissions: admissions@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7300. [12]

question: whats the difference between a minor and a certificate here

body.answer:
A minor is an undergraduate supplement to your major, intended to add depth and breadth. It must include 16–24 credits, counting non-General Education prerequisites and excluding lab science course credits. Courses for your primary or secondary major may overlap, but no more than half the minor’s credits may count toward the major. [4][6]

“Academic Certificates are organized, coherent programs of study usually comprised of credit-bearing courses.” They may also include non-credit learning experiences. Levels include undergraduate certificates, graduate certificates requiring at least 9 credits beyond the Bachelor’s level, and doctoral certificates requiring at least 12 credits beyond the Master’s level. They are not graduation requirements and are removed from the degree audit. [3]

Ramapo also distinguishes Professional Certificates: these consist entirely of not-for-credit learning experiences, are not differentiated by level, and are not noted on transcripts; the Registrar does not administer or issue them. [5]

For questions about how a particular certificate is recorded, contact the Office of the Provost at provost@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7330. [3][5]

question: What are the general education requirements for all students? I'm trying to figure out how many gen ed classes I would have to take outside my major if I did communication arts.

body.answer:
Ramapo’s general education curriculum is ten courses: four keystone courses, one in each of four keystone categories, and one course in two of three distribution categories. [3]
1. Keystone courses: First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102 (within the first 64 credits), and Studies in the Arts & Humanities. [3]
2. Keystone categories: one course each in Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning (within the first 64 credits). [3]
3. Distribution: one course in two of Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics. At least one course must be offered by a school other than the one housing your major. [3]
The catalog also lists Critical Reading and Writing II, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Global Awareness, plus two distribution categories. [4] Section 6 says that starting Fall 2026, the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools; section 3 says at least one distribution course must be offered by another school. The pages differ on that rule. [3][6]
For Communication Arts BA, the 2026–2027 recommended plan places General Education Requirement courses in several semesters, but does not specify how many gen ed classes must be taken outside the major. [1] The catalog says no more than two General Education courses may double count in both Gen Ed and the major. [5] The plan lists General Education categories and some major courses mapped to them; it is a recommended plan for students admitted during 2026–2027. [1]
For advising about which requirements remain, contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441. [2]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-COMM) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#waiver-of-general-education-requirements1) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/)

question: Is there a recommended course sequence for the elementary education certification track, like what to take each semester?

body.answer:
Yes. The recommended Graduation Plan is for Elementary Education students admitted during the 2026–2027 academic year. [1]

- First Year*, Fall (total 16 credits): INTD 101 - FIRST YEAR SEMINAR (4); SOCIAL SCIENCE INQUIRY (4); CRWT 102 - CRITICAL READING AND WRITING II (4); PSYC 101 - INTRODUCTION TO PSYCHOLOGY (4). [1]
- First Year*, Spring (total 16 credits): QUANTITATIVE REASONING – MATH 108 - ELEMENTARY PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS {recommended} (4); General Education Requirement (4); PSYC 215 - LEARNING, COGNITION, AND TEACHING (4); EDUC 211 - STUDENT LITERACY CORPS CE1 (Urban) (4); PATH 001 - CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 1. [1]
- Second Year**, Fall (total 16 credits): General Education Requirement (4); VALUES AND ETHICS – EDUC 221 - SOCIAL CONTEXT OF EDUCATION (4); General Education Requirement (4); SCIENTIFIC REASONING – BIOL 101 - INTRODUCTION TO BIOLOGY (recommended) (4); PATH 002 - CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 2. [1]
- Second Year**, Spring (total 16 credits): EDUC 222 - TEACHING: PRINCIPLES AND PRACTICES CE2 (Note: Must Be Fully Admitted to Teacher Education Program) (4); choose one: LITR 302 - GRAMMAR: THEORY AND PEDAGOGY or LITR 203 - METHODS OF LITERARY STUDY (HRS 4) or LITR 306 - LITERARY THEORY (HRS 4) (4); two Electives (Middle School Content for those interested) (4 each); PATH 003 - CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 3; EDUC 241 - INSTRUCTIONAL TECHNOLOGY (4). [1]
- Third Year, Fall (total 16 credits): Elective (Middle School Content for those interested) (4); Elective (PSYC 347 - ADOLESCENT PSYCHOLOGY) (for those interested in Middle School) (4); EDUC 360 - INTRODUCTION TO SPECIAL EDUCATION CE3*** with EDUC 301 - MEETING THE NEEDS OF ALL LEARNERS (co-req.) (4); choose one: LITR 308 - CHILDREN'S AND YOUNG ADULT LITERATURE or LITR 290 - TOPICS: (Permission Required) (DC for Culture/Creativity) (HRS 4) or LITR 279 - THE GRAPHIC NOVEL (HRS 4) (4). [1]
- Third Year, Spring (total 16 credits): General Education Requirement (4); MATH 210 - MATHEMATICS FOR ELEMENTARY EDUCATORS (4); SCIN 215 - SCIENCE FOR ELEMENTARY EDUCATORS (4); EDUC 346 - LITERACY THEORY & PRACTICE CE4 (Must have copy of substitute teacher license in TED account PRIOR to meeting with advisor) (4). [1]
- Fourth Year*****, Fall (total 16 credits): EDUC 370 - METHODS OF TEACHING ELEMENTARY MATHEMATICS CP1**** (4); EDUC 375 - METHODS OF TEACHING ELEMENTARY SCIENCE CP2**** (4); EDUC 365 - LITERACY ACROSS THE ELEMENTARY CURRICULUM CP3**** (4); EDUC 390 - TOPICS: CP4**** (4). [1]
- Fourth Year*****, Spring (total 12 credits): EDUC 490 - CLINICAL PRACTICE CAPSTONE: ELEMENTARY (12); upload Praxis II, substitute teacher license, current Mantoux/TB test to TED account PRIOR to meeting with advisor re. Clinical Practice. [1]

question: Can I double major in political science and law and society, and is there a minor in either one?

body.answer:
Yes. Political Science and Law and Society are both Bachelor of Arts majors [1][2], and undergraduates may pursue a second major [4]. With two majors, no more than half the courses may count toward both, and you must complete all writing-intensive courses required for the second major [5].

There is a Political Science minor [3]. I don’t have verified information about whether Ramapo offers a Law and Society minor. The Registrar is the office to check: reg@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7695 [8].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-BA-LAWS) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-BA-POLI) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-MN-POLI) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/declare-major-minor-certificate/)
